newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia mourns blast victims,rescue work nears end.
newsitem.headline: Russia mourns blast victims,rescue work nears end.

text.p: Flags flew at half-mast in Russia on Tuesday, a day of mourning for at least 67 people killed in a weekend explosion in the southern region of Dagestan, as rescuers gave up hope of finding any more survivors.
Itar-Tass news agency quoted the emergencies ministry as saying its rescue teams were halting the round-the-clock search launched after Saturday's blast in a military apartment block.
Tass said rescue workers had pulled 40 human survivors and an injured dog from the rubble of what once was a nine-storey concrete apartment block, home to families of border guards.
Eight people, including four children, were taken to hospital. Twenty children were among the dead.
"The chances of finding more survivors can be described as one-hundredth of one percent," Tass quoted Kamil Magomedov, head of the ministry's local branch, as saying.
Local officials said those parts of the building which survived the blast would be torn down, probably on Tuesday.

Some Moscow officials say the blast, in which the concrete panelled building collapsed like a pack of cards, was caused by a terrorist act, adding that separatist rebels from neighbouring Chechnya could have been to blame.
Rebel leaders, who are in the middle of peace talks with Moscow, denied any involvement but said they could not rule out that go-it-alone fighters carried out the blast.
Other officials say it is too early to come to definite conclusions as to what could cause the explosion.
Some suggested the blast followed a local mafia tiff or that explosives could have been stored in the building. The poorly constructed building would have been unable to withstand even a minor blast.

President Boris Yeltsin declared Tuesday a day of national mourning. He ordered flags to fly at half-mast across the country and asked mass media to cancel light entertainment programmes as a mark of respect.
